children: A large Xerox stockholder has called upon the company's board to take action to unlock shareholder value, including exploring the potential sale of all or part of a business unit.

Starteepo Sicav--a Prague-based alternative investment fund with a roughly 7.3% stake in Xerox--on Tuesday called for the workplace-technology company to be more transparent about the performance of its financial services unit, as well as consider strategic alternatives for the business.

"We remain supportive of the efforts the Board and management team have taken to improve Xerox's performance," Starteepo said in an open letter to Xerox's board, citing solid second-quarter results and increased full-year guidance as evidence the company's turnaround is gaining traction.
Despite the progress, though, Starteepo said it believes Xerox remains misunderstood and undervalued by the market.

"As a committed, long-term investor in Xerox, we believe the time is right for the Board and management to take bold action and unlock the value of a hidden gem: Xerox Financial Service," Starteepo wrote.

The investment fund estimated that XFS could be worth roughly $7.69 a share--or more than double the current share price of the entire company--with the right strategy in place and proper execution, based on precedent transactions.

Starteepo said Xerox needs to help investors better understand the business unit by providing more detail on its performance, and by more clearly communicating its current strategy. Beyond that, Starteepo called on the company's board to hire financial advisers to undertake a formal strategic review of the business.
